source.title: Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Deep Linear Residual Networks
source.authors: Lei Wu; Qingcan Wang; Chao Ma

record.tranche_reason: Tests a new initialization on nonlinear residual networks trained on Fashion-MNIST, including depths up to 10000; this is a new setting for the initialization and trainable-depth findings.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports theoretical convergence and numerical results for deep linear networks on target-matrix least-squares loss. Those results do not measure classification error. The nonlinear experiment uses 1000 Fashion-MNIST training samples; the accuracy results are shown in Figure 4.
record.test_reason: The study tests initialization-dependent optimization in deep linear networks and nonlinear residual networks. V4 specifically concerns activation-matched initialization and signal propagation in plain networks; the residual mZAS experiment does not test that version. The study also provides no comparison measuring any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors prove global convergence with a polynomial dependence on depth for ZAS-initialized deep linear networks and empirically demonstrate useful mZAS training of nonlinear residual networks, including depth 10000. The nonlinear result is experimental, without a corresponding convergence theorem.
record.recipe_differences: The nonlinear experiment uses modified ZAS, with zero residual-block weights and random V matrices, rather than the activation-matched or orthogonal initialization recipes in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and learning rate vary across the reported nonlinear residual-network runs; Xavier blows up at depths L=2000 and 10000, while mZAS is reported to optimize at L=10000.

fits_no_version.finding: With separately tuned learning rates on 1000 Fashion-MNIST samples, mZAS outperforms Xavier in nonlinear residual networks and successfully optimizes at depth 10000. Xavier diverges at depths 2000 and 10000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero-asymmetric initialization can improve optimization speed and trainable depth in nonlinear residual networks.

fits_no_version.finding: For deep linear networks, ZAS guarantees epsilon-optimal matrix-fitting loss in O(L^3 log(1/epsilon)) iterations under the stated learning-rate bound. Numerical comparisons show less saddle-region delay than near-identity initialization; only two of five near-identity runs escape within the plotted budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Asymmetric initialization can avoid saddle-region delays and enable polynomial-time optimization of deep linear networks.

record.problems: The nonlinear experiment uses only 1000 training samples from Fashion-MNIST. Figure 4 is the sole source for training-accuracy values, with no numeric values or uncertainty estimates stated in the text. Xavier and mZAS use different tuned learning rates, and the text does not specify a normalization comparison.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including label corruption and model-size or recipe comparisons.
Spurious-local-minimum frequency and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks.
Depth-related training degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified plain-tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in deep tanh networks; orthogonal convolution kernels at 10000 layers.
Recovery above the initial stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup matching normalized residual-network training.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V4 verdicts. Residual-network results do not establish the specified plain-network claim, and untested architectures or unavailable figure values are not scope-limiting evidence. The omitted linear results and deep-Xavier divergence fit no supplied version, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than missing.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, and the stated model-size and training-recipe comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem and spurious-minimum frequency as student width changes.
Plain-versus-residual comparison, depth-related training error, and normalization conditions.
Plain networks, activation-matched and orthogonal initializations, and orthogonal convolution kernels; the experiment instead tests modified ZAS against Xavier on nonlinear residual networks.
Learning rates above a stability threshold, curvature or sharpness, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparison, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup without normalization.
